Spec 120 (dispatched-run metrics, lifecycle #1055) makes implement and finalize runs write their own metrics records. Runs dispatched with the built-in token never fire the metrics `workflow_run` trigger, so their records used to wait for the daily sweep. Each wrapper now has a `persist-metrics` job that calls the existing `metrics-persist.yml` stage with the run's own id, with no App credentials and no concurrency group. Two optional, default-off stage inputs let it run in a cancelled run and keep it from failing the origin run. The record key already dedups against the `workflow_run` path and the sweep, and Gate 79 now checks the job's shape and has fixtures for each failure branch. The rollup comment gains a "Last daily sweep" line, and the spec adds a persisting-job contract and data model. Two exceptions are recorded, both accepted by the owner on 2026-11-08: finalize has no `started` gate, and a stalled queued job delays implement's persistence. 738c67b358a19bdaee086259482fcb9cf160a4a1.body:
Spec 122 (lifecycle issue #1094) makes the independent review of a spec pull request automatic. Once intake or clarify has announced a spec PR ready, with no `NEEDS CLARIFICATION` markers and the issue at `stage:spec`, a new `spec-pr-review.yml` workflow runs one review per head commit. The reviewer is Opus with the `code-review` recipe at high effort. It checks buildability against current main's permissions, secrets and variables, conflicts with the constitution and with merged specs' live contracts, and contradictory, untestable or undecided requirements. The result is posted on the PR as a verdict with structured findings. Owner-only decisions go back to clarify as questions with options, a recommendation and any precedent cited. The review is bounded by a round budget and the spec 116 convergence check, and it honours a `WING_COMMANDER_*_PAUSED` kill switch. The review never approves, requests changes or merges, so spec PR merge stays with the owner. The merge adds the decision module (`spec_pr_review.py`), the apply helper (`spec_pr_review_actions.py`), fixtures, and three gates (157 for the decision module, 158 for workflow wiring, plus registrations in gates 27, 68 and 93). It also adds a setup note in `docs/setup.md` and a fix so intake's `lifecycle issue: #N` line is the only source for the lifecycle issue. Plan PRs and final PRs are out of scope.

Spec 117 (implement stall hand-off and honest remaining-work reporting, lifecycle #992) changes how a lifecycle ends when implementation is not finished. Tasks that only a maintainer can perform (a real workflow dispatch, a repository variable change, a separate human-merged PR, a post-merge proof) are now marked as maintainer tasks and kept out of the phases implement must finish in order, so they no longer stall a cycle. The implement loop stops early only when a cycle names a concrete blocker in a validated `implement-blocker.json` field; otherwise it keeps running until the iteration cap, and every hand-off with implementation outstanding posts a stall comment with the outstanding count and reason. Finalize now renders its remaining-work report with separate "maintainer steps" and "unfinished implementation" sections, states when the lifecycle stalled, and drops standing instructions that are not discrete work items. The change is covered by a new gate, `verify-implement-stall-handoff.py`, with fixtures for the checkbox counter, outcome decision, blocker validation and remaining-work rendering.

b1680293a06fefdfff1f5ff8635a22be1b4aef0c.body:
Spec 116 (review loops that notice they aren't converging) landed in #1062 as part of the umbrella for lifecycle #994. Both automated review loops, the lifecycle review gate and the board loop, now compute convergence signals on every round in one module, `wc_convergence.py`, and from round 3 can stop early with a `not-converging` hand-off instead of spending the full five-round budget. The signals are: a finding count that did not fall, findings sitting on lines the loop itself wrote, a recurring finding, churn across consecutive rounds, and PR diff growth. Each round record now stores its diff size and a diff fingerprint, so growth survives a rebase and a rebase alone cannot re-arm a stopped loop. The lifecycle gate also no longer drops a recurring finding as already handled; it reports the recurrence and does not post `success`. The local `review-until-clean` skill uses the same arithmetic, and a new gate, `verify-convergence-single-home.py`, keeps that arithmetic in one place. The merge adds replay fixtures and tests for the signals and the loop wiring. The fold-time analyze check (Story 3) moved to proposal #1066, and the shared reviewer-procedure file (Story 5) is deferred.

Spec 121 lets the board loop work the Maintenance backlog (#889) one line at a time when no eligible issue is waiting. Each unchecked line is claimed with a short id the loop writes into it, then run through the same triage, route, fix, review and readiness steps as an issue. A fix that merges ticks the line with "(fixed by #PR)", and the backlog issue stays open. Lines that triage can close are ticked with the evidence quoted, lines that need a design decision are routed to a `spec-proposal`, and lines the loop cannot finish are held with a reason. The feature is off by default behind the `WING_COMMANDER_BOARD_BACKLOG_LINES` variable, and #889 is edited only through a read-modify-write helper (`board_backlog_edit.py`) that tolerates concurrent writers. The merge (#1121, closing lifecycle #1080) adds the helper, the line-selection module and its tests, the board-loop workflow changes, and gates `verify-board-backlog-edit.py` and `verify-board-backlog-lines.py`. It also adds a CLAUDE.md rule and the spec's contract, data model, plan, research and tasks documents.
